answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable sequence of modular squarings before it is accepted. Because every result depends on the preceding one, GPUs cannot split a single identity’s computation into parallel steps to reduce its elapsed time. An attacker may run clone-specific sequences concurrently, but each still incurs the sequential delay and computational cost—a bottleneck as persistent as a wharf, plume, or oasis is distinctive.
